body.title: Give every repository install the C++ standard fs-ext needs
body.reproduction:
In a fresh checkout on macOS with Node 22 and Apple clang 21, run `npm ci` at the repository root with no CXXFLAGS set.

Observed on 2026-11-10: the install stops while compiling fs-ext, with errors in the Node 22.22.1 V8 headers such as "no template named 'is_void_v' in namespace 'std'". The same command with `CXXFLAGS=-std=c++20` completes.

Expected: every supported way of installing the repository compiles fs-ext.

Not reproduced: the two GitHub workflows that run a bare `npm ci` use Ubuntu, where the failure has not been observed. A third workflow on Ubuntu already sets the flag.
body.rootCause: The project-memory package depends on the native package fs-ext, whose build file sets no C++ standard, so the compiler's default applies. Under Apple clang that default is too old for the Node 22.22.1 headers. The daemon install paths work around this by asking for C++17 through CXXFLAGS, through `NATIVE_CXX_STD` in the maintenance service and the install scripts, and the project-memory workflow does the same. The other install paths never got that setting: the main CI workflow, the root install in the VS Code plugin workflow, and the manual `npm install` in the build instructions.
body.fixIntent: Every supported way of installing the repository must ask for the same C++ standard the daemon install paths already use, so fs-ext compiles in CI and when a developer follows the build instructions. The daemon install paths keep their existing behaviour. The fix must confirm on macOS that a clean install with the documented command succeeds.

citations.quotedText: # install installs again. CXXFLAGS asks for C++17 (NATIVE_CXX_STD there): fs-ext
